newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Inc manages to raise profits on weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Japan Inc manages to raise profits on weak yen.

text.p: Japan Inc has shrugged off a weak economic recovery earlier in the year with many big companies posting higher profits for the interim period on the back of the weaker yen.

A corporate survey by the Wako Research Institute of Economics showed that nearly a third of Japan's big companies that have reported results so far posted six percent average growth in first-half profits compared with the previous year.
Wako based its figures on the parent interim current profits of 214 of the 766 companies in its survey. The other firms will release their results in the coming weeks.
All 766 firms are listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange and have business years ending on March 31, 1997. The list does not include banks, brokerages or insurance firms.
The after-tax parent interim profits of the 214 firms surged 20.21 percent against last year, while parent sales were up a more modest 5.86 percent, the research said.
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks.
The higher interim profits were largely attributed to the yen's retreat against the dollar.

Companies that rely heavily on export income have been hit especially hard by the yen's steep rise in recent years and the national recession that followed the bursting of the 1980s "bubble" economy of inflated asset prices.
With the yen's reversal and signs that the economy is finally emerging from the prolonged slump, Japanese companies are seeing a pick-up in demand and enjoying rising exports.
The dollar has rebounded from its post-war low of 79.75 yen in April last year to about 112 yen on Friday.
The weaker yen makes Japanese products more competitive and makes dollar-based overseas earnings cheaper to convert to yen.
Most Japanese car manufacturers and electric companies saw a healthy increase in half-year profits. But Wako said the oil, steel and non-auto transport sectors saw profits fall.
Consumer electronics giant Sony Corp saw half-year profits jump due to robust sales in its electronics and entertainment divisions, and said it expects the upward swing to continue.
Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd reported a 29 percent profit gain for the half-year, but said economic uncertainties cast a shadow on its second-half performance.
Electronics giant NEC Corp's first-half profits surged 31.6 percent as its telecommunications business overshadowed its slumping semiconductor operation.
But Japan Energy Corp blamed rising crude oil prices and a weak petrochemical product market for poor half-year profits, which fell 24 percent from a year earlier.
Major firms not included in the Wako survey also posted strong earnings for the first half.
Toyota Motor Corp said on Friday its interim current profits had jumped near four times year-on-year, while Nissan Motor Co Ltd said it had posted a healthy interim profit for the period.

Steelmakers reported mixed half-year earnings on Friday, saying profits had been hurt by Japan's slow economic recovery and high inventories. Industry leader Nippon Steel Corp said profits fell 3.2 percent for the period.
